question:
All managers are leaders. All leaders are communicators. Which conclusion definitely follows?
I. All managers are communicators.
II. All communicators are managers.
explanation: All managers → leaders → communicators, so I follows. Not all communicators need be managers, so II does not follow.

question: No laptop is a tablet. Some tablets are portable devices. Which conclusion is valid?

options.B: No portable device is a laptop
options.C: Some portable devices are not laptops

explanation: The tablets that are portable devices are not laptops (no laptop is a tablet), so some portable devices are not laptops.

question:
All A are B. Some B are C. No C is D. Which conclusion must be true?
I. Some A are C.
II. Some B are not D.
explanation: Some B are C and No C is D → those B's that are C are not D → Some B are not D (II). For I: A is a subset of B but those A's may all be non-C B's, so I doesn't necessarily follow.

question:
Some teachers are doctors. All doctors are graduates. Some graduates are rich. Which conclusions both follow?
I. Some teachers are graduates.
II. Some rich are graduates.
explanation: Some teachers are doctors + All doctors are graduates → Some teachers are graduates (I). Some graduates are rich → by conversion, Some rich are graduates (II).

question:
All pens write. No pencil writes. Some pencils are sharp. Which conclusions both follow?
I. No pen is a pencil.
II. Some sharp things are not pens.
explanation: No pencil writes + All pens write → No pen is a pencil (I). Some sharp pencils are not pens (since no pencil is a pen) → Some sharp things are not pens (II).

question: Some A are B. All B are C. Some C are D. No D is E. Which conclusion MUST be true?
explanation: Some C are D and No D is E → those C's that are D are not E → Some C are not E. A: A⊆C but may not overlap D. B: B's are C's but may not all be D's. D: A's may or may not be E's.

question: If it is raining, Ali carries an umbrella. Ali does not have an umbrella. What can you conclude?
explanation: Modus tollens: Rain → umbrella; no umbrella → no rain.

question: 'If X > 5, then Y > 10.' Given that Y ≤ 10, what can be concluded about X?
explanation: Contrapositive: ¬(Y > 10) → ¬(X > 5), i.e., Y ≤ 10 → X ≤ 5.

question: If Ahmed studies, he passes. If he passes, he gets a scholarship. Ahmed did not get a scholarship. What can we conclude?

options.A: Ahmed studied but did not pass
options.C: Ahmed passed but did not get the scholarship
options.D: Ahmed may or may not have studied

explanation: No scholarship → did not pass (contrapositive). Did not pass → did not study (contrapositive). Chain: ¬scholarship → ¬pass → ¬study.

question: If P then Q. If not-P then R. P is false. What can we conclude?
explanation: P is false → not-P is true → R is true (second rule fires). Q is indeterminate since the first rule only applies when P is true.

question: If the alarm rings, the dog barks. If the dog barks, the neighbours complain. The neighbours did NOT complain. What can you conclude?
explanation: Neighbours didn't complain → dog didn't bark (contrapositive). Dog didn't bark → alarm didn't ring (contrapositive).

question: 'Only if A is true is B true.' 'C is true only if B is true.' 'D is true if C is true.' A is false. Which must be true?
explanation: 'Only if A is B' means B→A. A is false → B must be false. 'C only if B' means C→B; B is false → C is false. 'D if C' means C→D; C is false so D is indeterminate. Only C is false is guaranteed.

question: Argument: Our new teaching method improves exam scores. Students using Method X scored 20% higher on average. Which most STRENGTHENS this conclusion?

options.A: Some students using Method X also had private tutors
options.B: Students who did NOT use Method X scored 20% lower on the same exam
options.C: Method X was developed by award-winning educators
options.D: Fifty students participated in the study

explanation: A control group without Method X scoring lower on the same exam directly supports that Method X — not other factors — caused the improvement.

question: Conclusion: The new advertising campaign increased brand awareness from 30% to 60%. Which most WEAKENS the claim that the campaign caused this increase?

options.A: The campaign used multiple media channels
options.B: The company launched three viral products during the same period
options.D: Brand awareness is an important business metric

explanation: Viral product launches provide an alternative explanation for the awareness rise, undermining the campaign as the sole cause.

question: Argument: Regular meditation reduces stress. A study of 200 adults found meditators had 30% lower cortisol levels. Which most WEAKENS this argument?

options.A: The study lasted only two weeks
options.B: Cortisol is a reliable biomarker for stress
options.C: Meditators in the study also exercised regularly and followed healthier diets
options.D: 200 adults is an adequate sample size

explanation: Confounding variables (exercise, diet) could explain lower cortisol, making meditation's causal role uncertain.

question: A company claims its new packaging reduced product damage by 40%. Which most STRENGTHENS the claim that packaging caused this reduction?

options.A: The new packaging is more expensive to produce
options.B: A control group using old packaging maintained the original damage rate during the same period
options.C: Customer satisfaction scores rose after the new packaging
options.D: The supply chain was restructured during the same period

explanation: A control group maintaining the old rate rules out external factors and isolates the packaging as the cause.

question: Argument: Installing air purifiers in schools improves student attendance. Schools with purifiers showed 8% higher attendance. Which most WEAKENS this?

options.A: Air purifiers are costly to maintain
options.B: Schools that installed purifiers were also in wealthier districts with better overall health resources
options.D: Attendance is a meaningful educational metric

explanation: Wealthier districts have better healthcare; the higher attendance may reflect socioeconomic advantage, not the purifiers.

question: A pharmaceutical company argues Drug Z reduces flu recovery time from 7 to 5 days based on a double-blind trial of 1,000 patients. Which finding most SERIOUSLY weakens this conclusion?

options.A: Some patients reported mild side effects from Drug Z
options.B: The placebo group's average recovery time was also 5 days
options.C: Patients taking Drug Z received nutrition counselling during the trial

explanation: If the placebo group also recovered in 5 days, Drug Z shows no advantage over placebo, entirely undermining the conclusion.

question: Students who score above 80% on mock tests will do well in the final exam. Hira scored 85%. Therefore, Hira will do well in the final exam. What assumption is being made?

options.A: Mock tests are harder than final exams
options.B: Mock tests reliably predict final exam performance
options.C: Hira studied harder for the mock than the real exam

explanation: The argument requires that mock test scores meaningfully predict final performance. Without this link the conclusion is unsupported.

question: Increasing the minimum wage will reduce poverty because workers will have more purchasing power. The argument assumes:

options.A: All workers currently earn below minimum wage
options.B: Employers will not reduce employment in response to higher wages
options.C: Poverty is solely caused by low wages
options.D: More purchasing power always reduces poverty without side effects

explanation: If employers cut jobs to offset higher wages, unemployment could rise and worsen poverty. Stable employment is a key unstated assumption.

question: Since this country exports more than it imports, its economy must be growing. The most critical underlying assumption is:

options.A: A trade surplus always leads to economic growth
options.B: Exports are more valuable than imports in absolute terms
options.D: The country has low domestic inflation

explanation: The argument directly assumes that a trade surplus equals growth. Without this causal link, the surplus proves nothing about overall economic expansion.

question: The city should ban single-use plastics to reduce ocean pollution, since most ocean plastic comes from land-based sources. The argument assumes:

options.A: Ocean pollution is harmful to marine ecosystems
options.B: Banning single-use plastics will significantly reduce land-based plastic reaching the ocean
options.C: Plastic is the only form of ocean pollution

explanation: The policy is only effective if the ban actually reduces plastic reaching the ocean. This causal bridge is the key unstated assumption.

question: Academic performance is the best measure of a student's potential. Therefore, universities should consider only academic grades in admissions. The assumption most critical to this argument is:

options.A: Universities have the legal right to set their own admissions criteria
options.B: Non-academic factors contribute no additional information about a student's potential
options.C: Academic grades are easy to compare across different schools
options.D: Students with high grades tend to succeed professionally

explanation: Excluding non-academic factors requires that they add nothing useful. If they did add predictive value, using only grades would be suboptimal.

question: A hospital's mortality rate increased after it hired more specialist doctors. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: The new specialist doctors were poorly trained
options.B: The hospital began accepting more critically ill patients that other hospitals refused
options.C: The hospital is located in a remote area
options.D: Mortality rates always rise temporarily when new staff join

explanation: Treating sicker patients naturally produces higher mortality regardless of doctor quality. The case mix changed, not the competence of care.

question: Country X's GDP per capita rose sharply, yet surveys show citizens report eating less nutritious food than a decade ago. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: GDP is not a reliable measure of national wealth
options.B: As incomes rose, people shifted to convenient processed foods and away from traditional home-cooked meals
options.C: Wealthier countries always have worse diets
options.D: The food supply decreased despite higher incomes

explanation: Rising incomes increase demand for convenience foods, which tend to be calorie-dense and nutrient-poor, explaining declining nutritional quality despite greater wealth.

question: A city reduced its total number of roads to cut traffic congestion, but traffic jams worsened. Which best explains this?

options.A: Traffic jams are random, unpredictable events
options.B: Fewer road options forced all vehicles onto the remaining roads, increasing density and congestion
options.C: People started driving more after the roads were removed

explanation: Eliminating roads without reducing vehicles forces all traffic onto fewer routes, increasing density — the opposite of the intended effect.

question: Students who attend private tutoring classes score lower on standardised tests than those who do not attend tutoring. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: Private tutors are less qualified than school teachers
options.B: Tutoring takes time away from independent study
options.C: Students with weaker academic performance are more likely to seek tutoring in the first place
options.D: Standardised tests are designed to disadvantage tutored students

explanation: Selection bias: struggling students seek tutoring. Their lower scores reflect pre-existing difficulty, not a negative effect of tutoring itself.

question: A government's major investment in new health clinics led to a documented INCREASE in disease prevalence in the region (confirmed by medical records). Which provides the most complete explanation?

options.A: The clinics were poorly staffed and spread infection
options.B: The government built clinics in the wrong areas
options.C: Better clinic access led more people to get tested, so previously undetected cases were now recorded, inflating recorded prevalence
options.D: The investment was too small to make a real difference

explanation: Increased testing reveals previously uncounted cases. Recorded prevalence rises even if actual disease burden is unchanged — a detection-bias effect.

question: A class has 40 students. 60% passed in Maths and 70% passed in English. What is the minimum number of students who passed in BOTH subjects?
explanation: Maths passers = 24, English passers = 28. Minimum overlap = 24 + 28 − 40 = 12 (inclusion-exclusion).

question: A company's quarterly revenue (Rs. millions): Q1=50, Q2=65, Q3=55, Q4=80. What is the percentage change from Q2 to Q3?
A survey of 500 people: 200 own a car, 150 own a bike, 80 own both. How many own NEITHER a car nor a bike?
Sales figures (Rs. millions): Product A=1.2, Product B=0.8, Product C=1.5, Product D=0.5. What percentage of total sales does Product C represent?
explanation: Total = 4.0M. Product C = 1.5/4.0 = 37.5%.

question: In a class of 120 students: 50 study Physics, 45 study Chemistry, 40 study Biology. 20 study Physics & Chemistry, 15 study Chemistry & Biology, 10 study Physics & Biology, 5 study all three. How many study exactly ONE subject?
explanation: Physics only=50−(20+10−5)=25. Chemistry only=45−(20+15−5)=15. Biology only=40−(15+10−5)=20. Total exactly one = 25+15+20 = 60.

question: Fatima, Hamza, Imran, Junaid, and Khaled sit in a row. Imran is in the middle. Fatima is immediately to Imran's left. Hamza is at the leftmost end. Khaled is at the rightmost end. What is Junaid's position from the left?
explanation: Middle of 5 = position 3 = Imran. Fatima=2, Hamza=1, Khaled=5, Junaid=4.

question: Six students P,Q,R,S,T,U sit in a row. Q is at position 4. P is at position 2. T is immediately left of Q. S is at position 1. U is immediately right of Q. R occupies the remaining seat. Who are Q's immediate neighbours?
explanation: S=1, P=2, T=3 (left of Q=4), U=5 (right of Q), R=6. Q's neighbours: T (left) and U (right).

question: Eight people sit in a row. Asim is 3rd from the left. Bilal is 5th from the right. How many people sit between Asim and Bilal?
explanation: Bilal = 8−5+1 = 4th from left. Asim = 3rd. Positions 3 and 4 are adjacent → 0 people between them.

question: Five books — History (H), Maths (M), Science (S), English (E), Urdu (U) — are on a shelf. E is at one end, H at the other end. S is immediately left of M. M is not adjacent to H. U fills the remaining position. What is the order from left to right?
explanation: E=1, H=5. S–M consecutive. M not adjacent to H (pos 5) → M≠4. So S=2, M=3, U=4. Order: E, S, M, U, H.

question: Ten people sit in a row. A is 4th from the left. B is 3rd from the right. C is exactly halfway between A and B. D is immediately to the right of C. E is 2nd from the left. How many people sit between E and D?
explanation: A=pos 4, B=pos 8, C=midpoint=(4+8)/2=pos 6, D=pos 7, E=pos 2. Between E(2) and D(7): positions 3,4,5,6 → 4 people.

question: Six people A,B,C,D,E,F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A is directly opposite D. B is directly opposite E. C is directly opposite F. B is immediately clockwise from A. Who is immediately counterclockwise from F?
explanation: Clockwise order: A(1),B(2),C(3),D(4),E(5),F(6). Counterclockwise from F(6) = E(5).

question: Six people P,Q,R,S,T,U sit around a circular table. P is directly opposite S. Q is immediately clockwise from P. R is immediately clockwise from Q. T is immediately clockwise from S. Who is immediately counterclockwise from S?
explanation: Clockwise: P(1),Q(2),R(3),S(4),T(5),U(6). Counterclockwise from S(4) = R(3).

question: Five people A,B,C,D,E sit around a circular table (seats 1–5 clockwise). B is at seat 1. A is 2 seats clockwise from B (seat 3). C is immediately clockwise from A (seat 4). D is immediately counterclockwise from B (seat 5). E occupies the remaining seat. Who is immediately clockwise from D?
explanation: B=1, E=2, A=3, C=4, D=5. Immediately clockwise from D(5) wraps to seat 1 = B.

question: Six people P,Q,R,S,T,U sit around a circular table (seats 1–6 clockwise). P is at seat 1. Q is 2 seats clockwise from P (seat 3). R is 2 seats clockwise from Q (seat 5). S sits directly opposite P (seat 4). T is immediately clockwise from R. U occupies the remaining seat. What are T's and U's seat numbers respectively?
explanation: P=1, Q=3, R=5, S=4, T=R+1=6, U=only remaining seat=2.

question: Pointing to a photograph, a man says 'She is the wife of the only son of my mother's husband.' How is the woman related to the man?
explanation: Mother's husband = his father. Only son of his father = himself. His wife = the woman in the photo.

question: M is the mother of N. O is N's brother. Q is married to N. R is the son of O. How is R related to Q's wife's mother?
explanation: Q's wife = N. N's mother = M. O is N's brother → shares mother M with N. R is O's son → R is M's grandson.

question: A is B's father. B and C are siblings. C is married to D. D is the parent of E and F. How is F related to A?
explanation: A is B's father; B and C are siblings → A is also C's father. C married D; their children are E and F. So A is F's maternal/paternal grandparent.

question: Starting from home, Raza walks 6 km North, then 8 km East. What is his straight-line distance from home?
explanation: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.

question: Layla starts from point X, walks 5m East, then 3m South, then 2m West, then 3m North. How far is she from X and in which direction?
explanation: Net East-West: 5−2 = 3m East. Net North-South: 3S−3N = 0. Final position: 3m due East of X.

question: In a certain code, TRAIN is written as VTCKP. Each letter is shifted by the same amount. What is the code for PLANE?
explanation: Each letter +2: T→V, R→T, A→C, I→K, N→P. PLANE: P→R, L→N, A→C, N→P, E→G = RNCPG.

question: In a code language: 'go fast slow' = '5 7 3', 'fast but sure' = '7 9 1', 'slow and sure' = '3 4 1'. What is the code for 'go'?
explanation: 'fast'=7 (common in sentences 1&2). 'sure'=1 (common in 2&3). 'slow'=3 (common in 1&3). Sentence 1: go, fast(7), slow(3) → codes 5,7,3 → go=5.

question: In a class of 30 students, Omar's rank is 8th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rank from bottom = 30 − 8 + 1 = 23.
